sections.subtitle: Dominion Energy Virginia (DEV), Dominion Energy South Carolina (DESC) and Contracted Energy

charts.title: 5-Year CapEx Plan by Segment ($m)
charts.annotation: Segments sum to roughly the blended CapexPlan5Yr KPI above; small cross-segment and corporate items are not separately charted.

segmentDelivery.title: Electricity delivered by segment
segmentDelivery.content:
Electricity delivered is retail volume (million MWh) sold to end-use customers by each regulated electric utility.

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: DEV (Virginia, serving most of the state plus part of North Carolina) delivers roughly four times the volume of DESC (South Carolina) -- DEV is the dominant rate base, and its data-center load growth is the main driver of both segments' forward capital plans.

What to watch:

  • DEV volume growth -- the data-center demand story management cites every quarter
  • Weather-driven swings between quarters (see CoolingDegreeDays/HeatingDegreeDays in the filings) versus the underlying trend

segmentCustomers.title: Customers by segment
segmentCustomers.content:
Customer counts (thousands of accounts) by regulated utility and service.

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: DEV serves roughly 2.8m electric customers versus DESC's ~0.8m electric and ~0.5m gas customers -- steady low-single-digit growth in all three is the base-load volume growth under the capital plan, distinct from the data-center-driven usage growth in the delivered-volume chart.

What to watch:

  • Customer growth rate versus population/economic growth in each service territory
  • Divergence between customer growth and delivered-volume growth (usage per customer)

capexPlanSegment.title: 5-year capital plan by segment
capexPlanSegment.content:
The disclosed 5-year capital plan split across DEV, DESC and the unregulated Contracted Energy (renewables) segment.

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: DEV absorbs the large majority of the plan -- transmission, grid and generation to serve Virginia's data-center corridor -- which is the rate-base growth that underpins the earned-ROE and EPS-growth guidance; DESC and Contracted Energy are smaller but still material swing factors.

What to watch:

  • Plan revisions year over year (growth or pullback in the DEV number specifically)
  • How much of Contracted Energy capex is merchant versus contracted/regulated-like

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Dominion Energy, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
